recipes.title: Universal Frittata
steps: 1. Preheat broiler.
2. Sauté fillings in cast iron skillet until tender.
3. Whisk eggs, milk, salt. Pour over fillings.
4. Cook on stovetop quiet until edges set (5-7m).
5. Broil 3-5m until golden and puffed.

recipes.title: Master Overnight Oats
steps: 1. Combine equal parts oats and liquid in a jar.
2. Shake well.
3. Refrigerate overnight.
4. Eat cold or warm up next morning.

recipes.title: Homestead Pancakes
steps: 1. Mix dry ingredients.
2. Mix wet ingredients.
3. Combine gently. Lumps are good.
4. Fry on hot greased griddle.

recipes.title: Liquid Gold Master Stock
steps: 1. Dump bones and scraps into large pot.
2. Cover with water.
3. Simmer 4-12 hours (stove) or 24h (slow cooker).
4. Strain and freeze.

recipes.title: Fridge Cleanout Soup
steps: 1. Sauté trinity in oil.
2. Add stock and tomatoes.
3. Add hard veg (potatoes), simmer 15m.
4. Add soft veg (corn/beans), simmer 5m.
5. Finish with vinegar and herbs.

recipes.title: Beef & Barley Stew
steps: 1. Coat beef in flour. Sear hard. Remove.
2. Sauté veg in beef fat.
3. Deglaze with wine.
4. Return beef. Add stock and barley.
5. Simmer covered low for 2 hours.

recipes.title: Creamy Potato Leek Soup
steps: 1. Sweat leeks in butter until soft.
2. Add potatoes and broth.
3. Simmer 20 mins until tender.
4. Blend until smooth. Season heavily.

recipes.title: Perfect Roast Chicken
steps: 1. Dry bird thoroughly.
2. Salt inside and out.
3. Place in cast iron skillet (on veg bed if using).
4. Roast at 425°F for 60-80 mins (165°F thigh).
5. Rest 15 mins before carving.

recipes.title: Pork Carnitas
steps: 1. Cut pork into chunks. Season.
2. Put in Dutch Oven with onion/orange/water.
3. Bake covered 300°F for 3 hours.
4. Uncover. Crank to 400°F to crisp fat (20m).

recipes.title: Ratio Meatloaf
steps: 1. Soak crumbs in milk.
2. Mix all ingredients gently.
3. Form loaf.
4. Bake 350°F for 60 mins.

recipes.title: Shepherd's Pie
steps: 1. Mix meat and veggies with gravy in baking dish.
2. Spread mashed potatoes on top. Seal edges.
3. Bale 400°F until gravy bubbles and potatoes brown.

recipes.title: No-Knead Artisan Bread
steps: 1. Mix shaggy dough. Cover. Wait 12-18 hours.
2. Preheat Dutch Oven to 450°F.
3. Drop dough into hot pot.
4. Bake covered 30 mins. Uncovered 15 mins.

recipes.title: Soft White Sandwich Loaf
steps: 1. Knead all ingredients 10 mins.
2. Rise 1 hr.
3. Shape and place in loaf pan. Rise 45m.
4. Bake 350°F for 30-35 mins.

recipes.title: Perfect Rice (Absorption)
steps: 1. Rinse rice well.
2. Boil water/rice. Cover tightly.
3. Low simmer 18 mins.
4. Remove from heat. Keep covered 10 mins (Crucial). Fluff.

recipes.title: Flaky Biscuits
steps: 1. Cut cold butter into flour/baking powder.
2. Stir in milk just until combined.
3. Pat out, fold over 3 times (creates layers).
4. Cut rounds. Bake 425°F for 12-15 mins.

recipes.title: 3:1 Vinaigrette
steps: 1. Whisk or shake in jar until creamy.

recipes.title: Béchamel (White Sauce)
steps: 1. Melt butter. Whisk in flour. Cook 1 min.
2. Slowly whisk in milk.
3. Simmer until thickened.

recipes.title: Pantry Marinara
steps: 1. Sauté aromatics.
2. Add tomatoes and herbs.
3. Simmer 20 mins.

recipes.title: Strawberry Jam (Canning)
steps: 1. Mix berries/pectin. Boil.
2. Add sugar. Hard boil 1 min.
3. Fill hot jars. 1/4 inch headspace.
4. Water bath process 10 mins.

recipes.title: Beef Jerky
steps: 1. Marinate meat 12-24 hours.
2. Dehydrate at 160°F for 4-6 hours.
3. Done when it cracks but doesn't snap.

recipes.title: Dried Apple Rings
steps: 1. Peel, core, slice.
2. Dip in lemon water to stop browning.
3. Dehydrate 135°F for 6-10 hours until leathery.

recipes.title: Sauerkraut
steps: 1. Shred cabbage.
2. Massage with salt until liquid releases.
3. Pack in jar under liquid weight.
4. Ferment 1-4 weeks.

recipes.title: Fermented Garlic Honey
steps: 1. Fill jar 3/4 with garlic.
2. Cover with honey.
3. Burp daily. Wait 1 month.

recipes.title: Lard Pie Crust
steps: 1. Cut lard into flour/salt.
2. Mix egg, vinegar, water. Pour into flour.
3. Mix until just combined. Don't overwork.
4. Chill 1 hour before rolling.

recipes.title: Skillet Cornbread
steps: 1. Melt drippings in cast iron skillet in 425°F oven.
2. Mix dry. Mix wet.
3. Combine.
4. Pour into hot skillet (listen for sizzle).
5. Bake 20 mins.

recipes.title: Chicken & Dumplings
steps: 1. Remove chicken from bone. Return meat to boiling broth.
2. Mix dough. Roll flat.
3. Cut into strips.
4. Drop into boiling broth.
5. Cover. Simmer 15 mins. Do not peek.

recipes.title: Bread & Butter Pickles
steps: 1. Salt veg and let stand 3 hours. Drain.
2. Boil brine (vinegar/sugar/spices).
3. Add veg. Heat to boil.
4. Pack hot jars. Water bath 10 mins.

recipes.title: Canned Applesauce
steps: 1. Cook apples in water until soft.
2. Mash or run through food mill.
3. Reheat to boil.
4. Pack hot jars.
5. Process 20 mins.

recipes.title: Zucchini Relish
steps: 1. Salt veg overnight. Drain and rinse.
2. Boil syrup of sugar/vinegar/spices.
3. Add veg. Simmer 30 mins.
4. Pack jars. Process 10 mins.

recipes.title: Survival Frittata
steps: 1. Preheat boiler (if available) or prepare skillet lid.
2. Whisk eggs and liquid distinctively.
3. Sauté mix-ins in an oven-safe skillet.
4. Pour egg mixture over mix-ins. Do not stir.
5. Cook on low heat until edges are set.
6. Transfer to oven/broiler to finish top, or cover with lid to steam.

recipes.title: Pantry Stir Fry
ingredients: Sauce: Soy sauce, sugar, vinegar, ginger
steps: 1. Mix sauce ingredients in a small cup.
2. Heat oil in wok or skillet until smoking.
3. Sear protein quickly. Remove.
4. Stir fry vegetables until crisp-tender.
5. Return protein and add carbs.
6. Pour sauce over everything and toss to coat.

recipes.title: Depression Era Pasta
steps: 1. Boil pasta in salted water. Reserve 1 cup water before draining.
2. In the same pot, sauté aromatics or mix-ins.
3. Add tomato sauce and heat through.
4. Toss pasta with sauce, adding reserved water to thin if needed.

recipes.title: Stone Soup
steps: 1. Brown any meat or bones in the bottom of the pot.
2. Add liquid and bring to a simmer.
3. Add sturdy vegetables (potatoes/carrots). Simmer 20m.
4. Add soft vegetables and grains. Simmer 15m.
5. Season aggressively.

recipes.title: Savory Oatmeal Bowl
steps: 1. Boil oats in salted liquid.
2. While hot, stir in an egg (it will cook in the oats) or top with fried egg.
3. Add soy sauce, sesame oil, or whatever savory condiments you have.

recipes.title: Red Beans & Rice
steps: 1. Sauté onion and pepper (and meat if using).
2. Add beans and cover with water by 2 inches.
3. Simmer until beans are creamy (1.5 - 2 hours).
4. Mash some beans against the side of the pot to thicken.
5. Serve over white rice.

recipes.title: Tuna Casserole
steps: 1. Boil noodles al dente.
2. Mix drained tuna, soup, peas, and noodles.
3. Pout into baking dish.
4. Top with crushed crackers.
5. Bake at 350F for 20-25 mins until bubbly.

recipes.title: Basic Sourdough Loaf
steps: 1. Dissolve starter in water.
2. Mix in flour and salt until shaggy dough forms. Rest 30m.
3. Perform 4 sets of 'Stretch and Folds' every 30 mins.
4. Bulk Rise: Let sit at room temp for 4-8 hours until doubled.
5. Shape into a round. Place in banneton/bowl. Fridge overnight.
6. Bake in Dutch Oven: 450F (20m lid on, 25m lid off).

recipes.title: Survival Hardtack
steps: 1. Mix ingredients into a very stiff dough.
2. Roll out to 1/2 inch thickness.
3. Cut into 3x3 squares.
4. Poke holes using a nail/chopstick (prevents puffing).
5. Bake 375F for 30 mins. Flip. Bake 30 mins more.
6. Cool completely. Should be hard as a brick.

recipes.title: Campfire Bannock
steps: 1. Mix dry ingredients.
2. Add oil and enough water to make a pliable dough.
3. Form into a patty (1 inch thick).
4. Fry in a greased skillet over coals, flip when golden.
5. PRO TIP: Can also wrap around a stick and roast.

recipes.title: Simple Yeast Bread
steps: 1. Bloom yeast in warm water with sugar for 5 mins.
2. Mix flour and salt. Add yeast water.
3. Knead 10 mins until smooth.
4. Rise 1 hour (doubled).
5. Punch down, shape loaf. Rise 30 mins.
6. Bake 400F for 30-35 mins.

recipes.title: Flour Tortillas
steps: 1. Cut fat into dry ingredients.
2. Add water, knead until smooth.
3. Divide into 8 balls. Rest 20 mins (Critical step!).
4. Roll paper thin.
5. Cook on HOT dry skillet, 30s per side (until bubbly).

recipes.title: Muscle Meat Jerky
steps: 1. Slice meat 1/4 inch thick. Remove ALL fat.
2. Marinate 12-24 hours.
3. Pat dry.
4. Dehydrate at 160F (or oven lowest setting door cracked) for 4-6 hours.
5. Done when it bends and cracks (white fibers visible) but doesn't snap.

recipes.title: Basic Sauerkraut
steps: 1. Shred cabbage finely.
2. Massage salt into cabbage until it releases liquid (brine).
3. Pack tightly into jar. Ensure cabbage is submerged in liquid.
4. Weigh down (bag of water or glass weight).
5. Ferment 3-4 weeks at room temp. Burp jar daily if needed.

recipes.title: Canned Tomatoes (Water Bath)
steps: 1. Score tomatoes, boil 1m, peel skins.
2. Pack into sterilized jars.
3. Add 1 tbsp lemon juice per pint (Critical for acid safety).
4. Leave 1/2 inch headspace.
5. Process in boiling water bath: 40 mins for pints, 45 for quarts.

recipes.title: Rabbit Stew
steps: 1. Dust rabbit pieces in flour, salt, pepper.
2. Brown in hot fat (bacon grease is best). Remove.
3. Sauté veggies.
4. Return rabbit, cover with cider/broth.
5. Simmer gently 1.5 - 2 hours until falling off bone.

recipes.title: Pan Fried Trout
steps: 1. Score skin of fish lightly.
2. Dredge in seasoned cornmeal.
3. Fry in hot butter/oil over medium heat.
4. 4-5 mins per side. Flesh flakes easily when done.

recipes.title: Venison Chili
steps: 1. Brown venison with onions.
2. Add spices and toast for 1 min.
3. Add remaining ingredients.
4. Simmer low and slow (venison is lean, don't boil hard).

recipes.title: Corned Beef Hash
steps: 1. Boil potato dice for 5 mins to soften. Drain.
2. Fry onion and potatoes in oil until starting to crisp.
3. Crumble in corned beef.
4. Press down with spatula to form crust. Flip and crisp other side.

recipes.title: Pantry Shakshuka
steps: 1. Sauté onion/garlic.
2. Add tomatoes and spices. Simmer 5 mins.
3. Make 4 divots in the sauce.
4. Crack eggs into divots.
5. Cover pan. Simmer 5-7 mins until whites set.

recipes.title: Lentil Tacos
steps: 1. Simmer lentils in water until soft (20m). Drain excess liquid.
2. Mash partially with fork.
3. Stir in taco seasoning.
4. Serve in tortillas.

recipes.title: Stovetop Rice Pudding
steps: 1. Combine rice, milk, sugar in pot.
2. Simmer medium-low, stirring often (scorches easily).
3. Cook until thickened (15-20m).
4. Add cinnamon/raisins off heat.

recipes.title: One Pot Chili Mac
steps: 1. Combine macaroni, chili, tomatoes, and 1 tomato-can of water in pot.
2. Bring to boil.
3. Simmer covered, stirring occasionally, until pasta is tender (10-12m).
4. Top with cheese if you have it.

recipes.title: Spam Musubi Bowl
steps: 1. Cut Spam into slices.
2. Fry until crispy.
3. Add splash of soy sauce and sprinkle of sugar to pan to glaze.
4. Serve glazed Spam over rice with crumbled nori.

recipes.title: Canned Fruit Cobbler
ingredients: 1 box Yellow Cake Mix (or flour/sugar/butter mix)
steps: 1. Pour fruit into baking dish.
2. Sprinkle dry cake mix over fruit.
3. Slice butter thinly and arrange over top.
4. Bake 375F for 35-40 mins until golden and bubbly.

recipes.title: Salmon Patties
steps: 1. Drain salmon.
2. Mix all ingredients. If too wet, add more crumbs.
3. Form into patties.
4. Pan fry in oil until golden brown on both sides.

recipes.title: Cowboy Caviar
steps: 1. Rinse all canned beans well.
2. Mix in bowl.
3. Toss with Italian dressing or vinegar/oil mix.
4. Serve as dip with chips or side salad.

recipes.title: Traditional Pemmican
steps: 1. Pound dried meat into a fluff/powder.
2. Melt tallow.
3. Mix meat powder and tallow 1:1 by weight.
4. Press into molds/blocks.
5. Will last years without refrigeration.

recipes.title: Refrigerator Pickles
steps: 1. Slice veggies into jars.
2. Boil vinegar, water, and salt to dissolve.
3. Pour hot brine over veggies.
4. Cool. Fridge. Ready in 24 hours.

recipes.title: Basic Lye Soap (Hot Process)
steps: 1. OUTDOORS: Add Lye to Water. (NEVER WATER TO LYE). Mix.
2. Melt fat. Coll lye and fat to ~100F.
3. Add Lye Water to Fat.
4. Stick lend to 'Trace' (pudding consistency).
5. Pour into mold. Insulate. Cut after 24 hours. Cure 4 weeks.

recipes.title: Peanut Butter Noodles
steps: 1. Boil noodles.
2. Whisk peanut butter, soy, sugar, and splash of hot water.
3. Drain noodles.
4. Toss hot noodles with sauce. Top with crushed peanuts/onions.

recipes.title: Loaded Baked Potato
steps: 1. Poke holes in potato. Bake 400F for 1 hour (or microwave 10m).
2. Slice open.
3. Top efficiently with heated chili and cheese.

recipes.title: Leftover Fried Rice
steps: 1. Heat oil in skillet until smoking.
2. Fry veggies.
3. Add rice (break up clumps). Fry until hot.
4. Push aside, scramble egg in empty spot.
5. Mix everything with soy sauce.

recipes.title: Three Bean Salad
steps: 1. Drain and rinse kidney beans. Drain others.
2. Mix beans.
3. Mix 1/2 cup vinegar, 1/4 cup oil, 1/4 cup sugar.
4. Toss beans with dressing. Marinade overnight for best taste.

recipes.title: Dandelion Green Salad
steps: 1. Harvest young greens before they flower (less bitter).
2. Wash thoroughly in cold water.
3. Toss with wild onion and dressing.

recipes.title: White Pine Needle Tea
ingredients: Handful White Pine Needles (flexible needles in clusters of 5)
steps: 1. Roughly chop needles to release oils.
2. Bring water to a boil, then remove from heat.
3. Steep needles for 5-10 mins (do not boil needles, it destroys Vitamin C).
4. Strain and drink.

recipes.title: Leached Roasted Acorns
steps: 1. Shell acorns and crush into large chunks.
2. Leach tannins by soaking in repeated changes of water until no longer bitter (takes 1-3 days).
3. Drain and pat dry.
4. Roast at 350F for 45 mins until fragrant and crunchy.
5. Grind into flour or eat as nuts.

recipes.title: Rocket Stove Corncakes
steps: 1. Mix cornmeal and salt. Pour boiling water over until a thick paste forms.
2. Let sit 5 mins.
3. Heat cast iron on rocket stove.
4. Fry thin patties in fat until crispy on both sides.

recipes.title: Haybox (Insulated) Rice
steps: 1. Bring rice and water to a rolling boil for 2 mins.
2. Immediately place tight lid on pot.
3. Place pot inside a haybox (box filled with straw/wool/blankets).
4. Seal box and wait 1 hour. Rice will cook using its own thermal mass.
5. Saves 15 mins of fuel.

recipes.title: Dry Cured Salt Pork
steps: 1. Rub pork thoroughly with salt/sugar mix.
2. Pack in a wooden box or crock with layers of salt between meat.
3. Store in cool, dark place (root cellar).
4. Over 2 weeks, moisture will be drawn out.
5. Keeps for 6-12 months. Soak in water to desalt before cooking.

recipes.title: Grandma's Fire Cider
steps: 1. Chop all aromatics and pack into a jar.
2. Cover with ACV.
3. Shake daily for 4 weeks.
4. Strain and mix with honey to taste.
5. Take a tablespoon daily for immunity.

recipes.title: Stinging Nettle Soup
steps: 1. Wear gloves to harvest and wash nettles.
2. Sauté onion and potatoes until soft.
3. Add broth and simmer 15 mins.
4. Add nettles. Cook 2-3 mins (cooking removes the sting).
5. Blend until smooth. Add cream if available.

recipes.title: Classic Pemmican
steps: 1. Pound dried meat into a coarse powder.
2. Mix meat and berries.
3. Pour hot melted tallow over mixture (1:1 ratio by weight).
4. Form into small bars. Let cool and harden.
5. Ultimate survival food; stores for years.

recipes.title: Sautéed Cattail Shoots
steps: 1. Harvest shoots from clean water source. Peel away outer green layers to find the white core.
2. Wash thoroughly.
3. Sauté in butter for 3-5 mins.
4. Taste is similar to cucumber or asparagus.
recipes.processing_note: Ensure cattails are harvested from clean, non-polluted water. See Guide 12.1 for ID and 12.4 for cleaning.

recipes.title: Roasted Chicory Coffee
steps: 1. Scrub roots clean. Dice finely.
2. Roast in oven (or by campfire) at low heat (250F) for 3-4 hours until dark brown and brittle.
3. Grind into a powder.
4. Brew like coffee. Naturally caffeine-free but bitter and robust.
recipes.processing_note: Scrub roots thoroughly. See Guide 12.4 for roasting and grinding details.

recipes.title: Ash-Roasted Potatoes
steps: 1. Poke holes in potatoes.
2. Wait for a fire to burn down to deep white hot ashes.
3. Dig a hole in the ash, bury potatoes, cover with 2 inches of ash.
4. Bake for 30-45 mins until soft when poked with a stick.
5. Brush off ash and eat with salt.

recipes.title: Elderberry Flu Syrup
steps: 1. Simmer berries and spices in water for 45 mins until liquid is reduced by half.
2. Strain out berries.
3. Let liquid cool to lukewarm (below 110F).
4. Stir in raw honey to keep enzymes alive.
5. Standard survival medicine for colds and flu.
recipes.processing_note: WARNING: MUST COOK berries to destroy cyanide precursors. Never eat raw. See Guide 12.4.

recipes.title: Anti-Inflammatory Golden Milk
steps: 1. Whisk all ingredients in a small pot.
2. Heat until steaming but not boiling.
3. Drink before bed for joint health and recovery.

recipes.title: Leached Acorn Pancakes
steps: 1. Mix dry ingredients.
2. Whisk in wet ingredients.
3. Fry on a hot griddle. Acorn flour adds a nutty, earthy flavor.
recipes.processing_note: Acorns MUST be leached to remove bitter/toxic tannins. See Guide 12.4 for leaching steps.

recipes.title: Wild Garlic Compound Butter
steps: 1. Mash wild garlic into butter.
2. Roll into a log using parchment paper.
3. Freeze or refrigerate. Use for flavoring meat and bread.

recipes.title: Sautéed Lamb's Quarters
steps: 1. Wash leaves thoroughly; remove tough stems.
2. Sauté garlic in oil.
3. Add greens and wilt for 2-3 mins. Nutrient-dense wild spinach substitute.

recipes.title: Rocket Stove Quick Stew
steps: 1. Bring broth to boil on rocket stove.
2. Add veggies and meat.
3. Simmer until veggies rehydrate.
4. Stir in potato flakes until desired thickness reached.

recipes.title: Solar Oven Sun-Bread
steps: 1. Place dough in a dark-colored pot with a lid.
2. Set solar oven in direct sun, adjusting every 30 mins.
3. Bake until internal temp reaches 190F (takes 2-4 hours depending on sun).
4. Very low fuel cost but requires clear skies.

recipes.title: Canned Spiced Beets
steps: 1. Boil beets until skins slip off.
2. Slice or leave whole (if small).
3. Pack into jars. Cover with hot brine (vinegar/sugar/spices).
4. Water bath process 30 mins.

recipes.title: Potted Beef (Confit)
steps: 1. Slow roast beef until falling apart.
2. Shred beef finely. Mix with juices and some melted fat.
3. Pack tightly into jars. Cover top with 1 inch of pure melted fat.
4. Once fat hardens, it seals out air. Store in cold root cellar.

recipes.title: Burdock Root & Beef Stew
steps: 1. Sauté meat and onion.
2. Add burdock root. Burdock is very fibrous; needs long simmering.
3. Cover with broth. Simmer 1 hour until root is tender. Nutty, artichoke-like flavor.
recipes.processing_note: Peel thick skin before cooking. See Guide 12.4 for digging and prep.

recipes.title: Primitive Cattail Flour
steps: 1. Dig roots from clean mud. Scrub clean.
2. Peel bark to reveal starchy core.
3. Mash cores in a bucket of water. Starch will settle at bottom.
4. Pour off water. Dry the white sludge into flour.
5. Use 1:1 with wheat flour for survival bread.
recipes.processing_note: Harvest from clean water. Refer to Guide 12.4 for the starch settling method.

recipes.title: Rose Hip Jam (Vitamin C)
steps: 1. REMOVE ALL SEEDS from hips (they have irritating hairs).
2. Simmer hips in water until soft.
3. Mash and add sugar.
4. Boil until thick. Extremely high in Vitamin C.
recipes.processing_note: MANDATORY: Remove all seeds and irritating hairs. See Guide 12.4 for removal technique.

recipes.title: Ash-Roasted Corn in Husk
steps: 1. Soak whole ears in water for 10 mins (prevents burning).
2. Place directly on hot coals. Cover with ash.
3. Rotate every 5 mins.
4. Peel back charred husks; corn will be perfectly steamed.

recipes.title: Hot Stone Broth
steps: 1. Heat clean stones (NOT sandstone/wet rocks) in fire until glowing.
2. Place water and ingredients in a wooden bowl or skin bag.
3. Drop hot stones into water one by one Using tongs/sticks.
4. Water will boil instantly. Replace stones as they cool until food is cooked.

recipes.title: Pickled Garlic Cloves
steps: 1. Pack garlic into small jars.
2. Boil vinegar/salt brine.
3. Pour over garlic. Water bath process 5 mins or keep in fridge.
4. Mellows the garlic; prevents botulism in oil storage.

recipes.title: Salt-Cured Egg Yolks
steps: 1. Bury yolks in salt/sugar mix in a container.
2. Refrigerate (or root cellar) for 4 days.
3. Remove and rinse. Dry in low oven or dehydrator until firm like parmigiano cheese.
4. Grating over pasta/rice adds intense savory flavor.

recipes.title: Elderflower Fritters
steps: 1. Whisk flour, egg, and liquid into a thin batter.
2. Dip flower clusters into batter, holding the stem.
3. Fry in hot oil until golden (about 1 min).
4. Snip off the stems and serve with honey.

recipes.title: Purslane & Egg Stir-fry
steps: 1. Wash purslane; use stems and leaves.
2. Sauté garlic.
3. Add purslane and stir-fry for 1 min.
4. Add beaten eggs and scramble until set. High in Omega-3 fatty acids.

recipes.title: Roasted Groundnuts (Apios)
steps: 1. Harvest tubers from wet areas. Scrub well.
2. Boil for 10 mins (helps soften the skin).
3. Toss with oil and salt.
4. Roast at 400F for 20 mins until crunchy outside and potato-like inside.

recipes.title: Spit-Roasted Rabbit
steps: 1. Rub rabbit with salt and wild garlic.
2. Skewer on a green (unseasoned) hardwood branch.
3. Suspend over hot coals (not flames).
4. Rotate slowly for 45-60 mins until juices run clear. Baste with fat if available.

recipes.title: Skillet Soda Bread
steps: 1. Mix dry. Add liquid until it forms a shaggy dough.
2. Form into a flat disc.
3. Place in a preheated cast iron skillet with a lid.
4. Bake over medium heat (or in coals) for 12 mins per side.

recipes.title: Canned Pickled Pike/Bass
steps: 1. Soak fish in salt brine for 24 hours. Rinse.
2. Pack into jars with onion slices.
3. Cover with boiling vinegar/sugar/spice brine.
4. Water bath process 15 mins. Wait 1 week for flavors to develop and bones to soften.

recipes.title: Survival Mushroom Powder
steps: 1. Slice mushrooms paper thin.
2. Dehydrate at 125F until brittle.
3. Grind in a mortar and pestle into a fine powder.
4. Store in airtight jars. Adds incredible umami/protein to any soup or stew.

recipes.title: Traditional Birch Syrup
steps: 1. Tap birch trees in late spring. Sap is lower sugar than maple (100:1 ratio).
2. Boil sap in a large flat pan over high fire.
3. As it thickens, lower heat significantly. Birch syrup burns easier than maple.
4. Bottle when it reaches 66% sugar content. Dark, spicy, and mineral-rich.
recipes.processing_note: Birch sap spoils quickly. Process immediately. See Guide 12.4 for tapping safety.

recipes.title: Survival 'Joe's' Mead (Quick)
steps: 1. Shake honey and warm water in a jug until dissolved.
2. Add orange, raisins, and yeast.
3. CAP LOOSELY or use a balloon with a pinhole (to let CO2 escape).
4. Ferment in dark place for 2 months.
5. Syphon off the clear liquid. Potent and easy.

recipes.title: Wild Sumac 'Lemonade'
steps: 1. Rub sumac clusters in cold water to release tart malic acid. Do not use hot water (it releases bitter tannins).
2. Strain through cheesecloth to remove fine hairs.
3. Sweeten to taste. High in Vitamin C and very refreshing.
recipes.processing_note: Use ONLY cold water to avoid bitter tannins. See Guide 12.4 for ID vs Poison Sumac.

recipes.title: Viking Pine Bark Bread
steps: 1. Harvest the white, soft inner bark from a fallen or thinned pine tree. Do not girdle live trees.
2. Dry the bark and grind into a fine flour.
3. Mix 1 part bark flour to 2 parts wheat flour.
4. Add water/salt to form dough. Bake as flatbreads. Rescued many through winter famines.
recipes.processing_note: Ethical harvesting is critical. Harvest Cambium layer only. See Guide 12.4 for prep.

recipes.title: Cast Iron Campfire Pizza
steps: 1. Heat oil in a heavy cast iron skillet over coals.
2. Lay dough in skillet. Fry for 3-5 mins until bottom is brown.
3. Flip dough. Quickly add toppings.
4. Cover skillet with a lid or foil. Place hot coals on top of lid to melt cheese from above.

recipes.title: Clay-Baked River Fish
steps: 1. Stuff fish with onions. Leave scales on.
2. Coat the entire fish in a 1-inch layer of wet clay.
3. Place the clay 'brick' directly into hot coals.
4. Bake for 30 mins. Crack open the clay; the scales and skin will peel off with the clay, leaving perfectly steamed flesh.

recipes.title: Simple Dried Apple Rings
steps: 1. Slice apples into thin rings. Dip in lemon water.
2. String onto a line or layout on racks.
3. Dry near a woodstove or in the sun until leathery and no moisture remains.
4. Keeps for months in jars.

recipes.title: Honey & Onion Cough Syrup
steps: 1. Slice onion thinly. Layer in a jar with honey.
2. Let sit overnight at room temp. The honey will draw out the onion juice.
3. Strain. Take a spoonful for coughs and sore throats. Very effective antibacterial properties.

recipes.title: Willow Bark Tea (Natural Aspirin)
ingredients: 1 tsp Dried White Willow Bark (inner bark)
steps: 1. Harvest inner bark from willow twigs. Dry and crush.
2. Simmer 1 tsp bark in water for 10-15 mins.
3. Contains salicin, the precursor to aspirin. Drink for pain relief and fever reduction.

recipes.title: Chickweed & Walnut Pesto
steps: 1. Wash chickweed thoroughly. It is a mild, corn-like flavored green.
2. Blend or crush nuts and garlic.
3. Add chickweed and oil. Blend until smooth.
4. Use over pasta or as a bread spread. High in vitamins.

recipes.title: Daylily Bud Fritters
steps: 1. Harvest buds when firm and green/orange but not open.
2. Dip in batter.
3. Fry in shallow oil until golden.
4. Taste is similar to green beans or okra.

recipes.title: Sweet Ash-Roasted Onions
steps: 1. Place whole onions directly into hot ashes/coals.
2. Roast for 20 mins until the outer skins are black and charred.
3. Pull from fire. Peel away the burnt layers.
4. The inner heart will be sweet, steamed, and perfectly cooked.

recipes.title: Solar Oven Brownies
steps: 1. Mix batter and pour into a thin dark metal pan.
2. Place in solar oven. Align with sun.
3. Bake 1.5 - 3 hours depending on solar intensity.
4. Passive cooking that keeps the 'kitchen' cool in summer.

recipes.title: Pickled Garlic Scapes
steps: 1. Chop scapes into 2-inch lengths.
2. Pack into jars.
3. Pour hot pickling brine over scapes.
4. Water bath process 10 mins. Crunchy, mild garlic flavor.

recipes.title: Traditional Survival Mincemeat
steps: 1. Combine all ingredients in a large pot.
2. Simmer for 1 hour to integrate flavors.
3. Pack into jars. The high sugar/acid/fat content preserves the meat for winter.
4. Traditionally used for pies but can be eaten as a high-calorie energy food.

recipes.title: Quick Dandelion Wine
steps: 1. Steep petals in hot water for 2 days.
2. Strain. Add sugar and yeast.
3. Ferment in a jug with an airlock.
4. Bottle after 2 months. Best after 6-12 months. Sunny and floral.

recipes.title: Charcoal Tummy Biscuits
steps: 1. Mix ingredients into a stiff dough.
2. Roll thin and cut into crackers.
3. Bake until dry and hard.
4. Eat 1-2 when experiencing stomach upset or bloating. Home-made charcoal must be made from clean hardwood.

recipes.title: Wild Garlic Mustard Pesto
steps: 1. Garlic mustard is an invasive species; harvest as much as you want.
2. Blanch leaves for 30s to reduce bitterness (optional).
3. Pulse all ingredients in a blender.
4. Sharp, garlicky, and peppery. Great for foraged pizza.

recipes.title: Cattail Pollen Gold Cakes
steps: 1. Shake yellow pollen from cattail heads in early summer.
2. Sift out any bugs/fluff.
3. Mix with flour and standard pancake wet ingredients.
4. The pollen adds a beautiful gold color and a sweet, floral nutty taste.

recipes.title: Hot Stone Tea
steps: 1. Heat clean stones in fire.
2. Place water and herbs in a wooden or wax-coated container.
3. Add hot stones until steaming. Effectively brews tea without needing a metal pot.

recipes.title: Dutch Oven Coal-Bread
steps: 1. Pre-heat Dutch oven in coals.
2. Dust bottom with cornmeal. Add dough.
3. Place lid on. Cover lid with 2 inches of hot coals.
4. Place 3-4 small coals underneath the oven.
5. Bake for 30-45 mins. The 'coals-on-top' method mimics a kitchen oven perfectly.

recipes.title: Old World Salted Herring
steps: 1. Clean fish but leave bones in (they soften).
2. Layer fish and salt 1:1 in a wooden barrel or ceramic crock.
3. Press down with a weight.
4. Brine will form. Leave for 2 weeks. Keeps for 1 year in cool storage. Soak in water for 24h before eating.

recipes.title: Pressure Canned Chicken
steps: 1. Pack raw chicken tightly into clean jars. Leave 1 inch headspace.
2. Add 1/2 tsp salt per pint. Do not add liquid (it makes its own broth).
3. Process at 11 lbs pressure (adjust for altitude): 75 mins for pints, 90 mins for quarts.
4. Safe, shelf-stable meat for years.

recipes.title: Fire & Onion Tonic
steps: 1. Grate onion into honey.
2. Add a heavy pinch of cayenne.
3. Take by the spoonful for severe congestion and sore throats.

recipes.title: Staghorn Sumac Spice (Za'atar style)
steps: 1. Harvest red sumac heads in late summer.
2. Dry thoroughly in a solar dehydrator.
3. Pound in a mortar and pestle to remove the fuzzy red coating from the hard seeds.
4. Sift to keep only the red powder.
5. Tangy, lemony spice that keeps for years. Great on meat or in hummus.

recipes.title: Eastern White Cedar Tea
steps: 1. Steep a small amount of cedar leaves in hot water (do not boil).
2. Very high in Vitamin C. Use sparingly; do not drink daily as it can be hard on kidneys in large amounts.
3. Survival classic for preventing scurvy in winter.

recipes.title: Flatbread on a Hot Rock
steps: 1. Find a large, flat, clean stone (granite is best; avoid river rocks).
2. Heat the stone in the fire until it sizzles when touched with water.
3. Scrape off ash. Lay thin dough discs directly on the rock.
4. Flip when the edges curl. Perfectly charred primitive bread.

recipes.title: Solar Oven Berry Muffins
steps: 1. Pour batter into a dark muffin tin.
2. Place in solar oven for 1.5 - 2 hours.
3. Muffins stay incredibly moist due to the low-temp steam environment of the solar cooker.

recipes.title: Salt-Cured Quail Eggs
steps: 1. Bury raw eggs (in shell) in a container of salt.
2. Wait 3-4 days. The salt draws moisture through the shell, curing the egg inside.
3. To eat, boil briefly or bake. The texture is firm and the flavor intensified. Keeps for weeks without refrigeration.

recipes.title: Pickled Wild Mushrooms
steps: 1. Pre-boil mushrooms to ensure safety and remove excess moisture.
2. Pack into jars with aromatics.
3. Cover with boiling vinegar/oil/salt mixture.
4. Water bath process 10 mins. Gourmet survival staple.

recipes.title: Fermented Honey Garlic
steps: 1. Fill a jar with garlic cloves. Cover with raw honey.
2. Flip jar daily. It will bubble as it ferments.
3. After 2 weeks, garlic is soft and honey is thin/infused.
4. Nature's strongest antibiotic. Eat a clove at the first sign of illness.

recipes.title: Spit-Roasted Partridge
steps: 1. Season the bird inside and out with salt, pepper, and herbs.
2. Truss the bird or skewer it onto a spit.
3. Roast over medium coals, turning frequently.
4. Baste with butter or oil until skin is crisp and meat is just cooked through (approx 15-20 mins).

recipes.title: Crispy Partridge Fingers
steps: 1. Slice partridge breasts into uniform strips.
2. Dip strips into beaten egg, then coat thoroughly in seasoned flour or breadcrumbs.
3. Heat oil in a skillet over medium-high heat.
4. Fry strips for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy.

recipes.title: Braised Partridge with Cabbage
steps: 1. Brown the partridges in a dutch oven with fat or bacon.
2. Remove birds, add onion and carrots, and sauté until soft.
3. Add cabbage and stir to coat.
4. Return birds to the pot, add stock, and cover.
5. Simmer on low heat for 1 to 1.5 hours until meat is tender.

recipes.title: Homestead Rabbit Stew
steps: 1. Brown rabbit pieces in a heavy pot.
2. Add onions and carrots, sauté for 5 mins.
3. Add liquid and bay leaf. Bring to a boil, then reduce to simmer.
4. Add potatoes after 1 hour.
5. Simmer till meat falls off the bone (usually 2 hours).

recipes.title: Pan-Fried Wild Rabbit
steps: 1. Season flour with salt, pepper, and paprika.
2. Dip rabbit pieces in milk, then dredge through the seasoned flour.
3. Heat lard in a large skillet until hot.
4. Fry rabbit pieces on medium heat, turning to ensure even browning (approx 20-30 mins total).

recipes.title: Rabbit Confit
ingredients: Lard or Duck Fat (enough to cover)
steps: 1. Salt the rabbit pieces and let sit for 1 hour. Rinse and pat dry.
2. Place meat in a deep baking dish with herbs and garlic.
3. Melt fat and pour over meat until completely submerged.
4. Cook at 225°F for 3-4 hours until meat is incredibly tender.
5. Store in the fat to preserve, or sear in a pan to serve.

recipes.title: Classic Brunswick Stew
steps: 1. Simmer squirrels in water until meat is tender enough to de-bone.
2. Remove meat, discard bones, and return meat to broth.
3. Add all vegetables and simmer on low for another 2 hours.
4. Season with salt, pepper, and a dash of hot sauce if desired.

recipes.title: Smoked & Braised Squirrel
steps: 1. Smoke squirrels at 225°F for 1.5 hours to infuse flavor.
2. Transfer to a pot with onion, cider, and honey.
3. Cover and braise on low for another 2 hours until tender.
4. Shred the meat for tacos or sliders.

recipes.title: Roasted Dandelion Coffee
steps: 1. Scrub roots clean and chop into small uniform pieces.
2. Roast in a skillet or oven at 350°F until dark brown and aromatic.
3. Grind the roasted roots into a coarse powder.
4. Brew like regular coffee (1 tbsp per cup of water).

recipes.title: Master Acorn Flour
steps: 1. Shell the acorns and grind the nutmeats into a coarse meal.
2. Place in a cloth bag and submerge in running water or change water multiple times until bitterness (tannins) is gone.
3. Spread the leached meal on a tray and dry thoroughly in a low oven or sun.
4. Grind into a fine flour and use 1:1 with wheat flour in recipes.

recipes.title: White Pine Needle Tea
steps: 1. Strip needles from branches. Avoid the brown ones.
2. Chop needles into small pieces to release oils.
3. Steep in hot (not boiling) water for 5-10 minutes.
4. Strain and drink for a massive dose of Vitamin C.

recipes.title: Wild Rose Hip Jelly
steps: 1. Simmer rose hips in water until soft. Mash and strain through a fine jelly bag.
2. Measure 3 cups of the rose hip juice into a pot.
3. Add pectin and lemon juice, bring to a hard boil.
4. Add sugar and boil for 1 minute. Skim foam.
5. Process in a water bath for 10 minutes.

recipes.title: Wild Cattail 'Asparagus'
steps: 1. Pull young cattails from the marsh. Peel back the outer layers to reach the white core.
2. Slice into 4-inch pieces.
3. Sauté in butter with salt and pepper for 5-7 minutes until tender.
4. Tastes like a cross between cucumber and asparagus.

recipes.title: Wild Burdock Root Stew
steps: 1. Sauté meat and onions in a pot.
2. Add burdock root, carrots, and enough water to cover.
3. Simmer for 45-60 minutes until roots are tender like parsnips.
4. Season with soy sauce for an earthy, deep flavor.

recipes.title: Slow-Roasted Venison Leg
steps: 1. Make small slits in the meat and insert garlic slivers.
2. Rub with salt, pepper, and chopped herbs.
3. Sear in a hot pan, then transfer to a roasting dish with stock and wine.
4. Roast at 300°F until internal temp reaches 135°F for medium-rare.
5. Rest for at least 20 minutes before carving.

recipes.title: Traditional Moose Jerky
ingredients: 2 lbs Moose Lean Meat (sliced thin across grain)
steps: 1. Mix marinade ingredients and coat meat slices thoroughly.
2. Refrigerate for 12-24 hours.
3. Arrange slices on dehydrator racks or a low oven (160°F).
4. Dry for 6-10 hours until meat is leathery but still bendable.
5. Store in airtight jars for long-term survival protein.

recipes.title: Wild Duck with Orange & Honey
steps: 1. Prick the duck skin to help fat render.
2. Mix orange juice, honey, soy, and zest into a glaze.
3. Roast ducks at 350°F, brushing with glaze every 15 minutes.
4. Remove when skin is dark mahogany and crisp.
5. Let rest. Meat should be slightly pink.

recipes.title: Pheasant Normande
ingredients: 1 cup Heavy Cream or Apple Cider
steps: 1. Brown pheasant pieces in butter and remove.
2. Sauté apples in the same pan until golden.
3. Return pheasant, add cider/cream, and cover.
4. Simmer until meat is tender (approx 45 mins).
5. Serve with the creamy apple sauce.

recipes.title: Fermented Garlic Honey
steps: 1. Fill a clean jar about 2/3 full with peeled garlic cloves.
2. Pour honey over the garlic until completely covered.
3. Close the lid and flip the jar to coat everything.
4. Loosen the lid daily to release built-up gases (burping).
5. Flip daily for 2 weeks. The honey will become runny and the garlic will darken.

recipes.title: Pine Pitch Drawing Salve
steps: 1. Melt the oil/lard in a double boiler (or a tin can in hot water).
2. Add the resin and stir until dissolved. Use a stick you can throw away.
3. Strain through a fine mesh or cheesecloth to remove bark/bugs.
4. Add beeswax for a firmer texture and charcoal to aid 'drawing' action.
5. Pour into a small tin. Apply to splinters, boils, or minor infections.

recipes.title: Survival Master Tonic (Fire Cider)
steps: 1. Place all solid ingredients into a quart jar.
2. Fill with apple cider vinegar until completely covered.
3. Use parchment paper under the lid to prevent corrosion.
4. Shake daily for 4 weeks.
5. Strain through cheesecloth and keep the liquid. Take a shot daily for immunity.
